history.summary: IMPORTANT IDENTITY NOTE: No published travel, tourism, or temple source documents a specific 'Kalibari Temple' in Bishnupur, Manipur; the identity, exact location, age, and history of this shrine could not be verified from web sources, so this entry is provisional (verify). All web results for 'Bishnupur' + 'Kali/Kalibari' point to West Bengal: the Kaal Bhairab temple at Bishnupur Bankura (722122), Siddheswari and Tilbari Kali Mandirs at Bishnupur (WB), and Bishnupur Kali Bari at Berhampore, Murshidabad (WB) - none in Manipur. Manipur tourism listings for Bishnupur (tourmyindia, travelsetu) name only the Vishnu Temple and pre-Hindu shrines (Ibudhou Thangjing, Konung Lairembi, Ibudhou Pakhangba Khubam); no Kalibari appears. Bishnupur (Manipur) is an old Vaishnavite pilgrimage town, so a small community Kali shrine could exist but is undocumented - do not conflate this entry with the West Bengal Kali shrines above. town_description: Bishnupur (Lamangdong in ancient times) is the headquarters of Bishnupur district, Manipur, about 27 km south of Imphal on the Tiddim Road (24.6333N, 93.7667E per Wikipedia). It derives its name from the ancient 15th-century Vishnu temple. The bustling town is known for stoneware production, hill-grown oranges, yongchak (tree beans), vegetables and shoibum (fermented bamboo shoot); nearby attractions include Loktak Lake, Keibul Lamjao National Park and the Loukoipat ecological park.
